nodes.title: Homotopy pro-local systems
nodes.statement: Specialize D0’s size-controlled Pro category to simplicial sets, with pointed objects represented by compatible actual vertices. A local system on X=(X_i) is a local system on one level, modulo pullback to a later level; its morphisms use the corresponding filtered colimit. The homotopy pro-local system Π_nX consists of the ordinary fundamental-groupoid homotopy local systems on the levels. For a pointed representative put π_n(X,x)=(π_n(X_i,x_i)); π_0 is pro-set-valued, π_1 pro-group-valued, and π_n is pro-abelian for n≥2. Connected means isomorphic to a levelwise connected diagram. This does not mean that its homotopy limit is path-connected.
hypotheses: Small cofiltered presentations in fixed universes; ordinary simplicial homotopy supplied by AlgebraicTopology.

sources.match: The local-system formulation handles components and basepoint transport before reducing to the connected pointed case.

proofSteps: Use the imported Pro carrier and finite-diagram reindexing; retain the universe of the indexing category.
Pull local systems back along transition maps and pass to the filtered colimit category. Ordinary homotopy groups and their path transport come from AlgebraicTopology.
Define the homotopy pro-local systems with their transition morphisms, and compare evaluation at a compatible vertex with the levelwise π_n system.
acceptance: The hypotheses and the indicated canonical map are retained under every use.

nodes.title: Isaksen homotopy model structure
nodes.statement: On Pro(SSet), take weak equivalences to be maps inducing an isomorphism of π_0 and of every homotopy pro-local system Π_nX→f*Π_nY, n≥1. Cofibrations are essentially levelwise monomorphisms, and fibrations have the right lifting property against trivial cofibrations. These classes form Isaksen’s simplicial model structure and induce its pointed model and homotopy categories. Every object is cofibrant. Its strict predecessor instead inverts essentially levelwise ordinary weak equivalences. Factorizations here are not asserted functorial.
hypotheses: Small cofiltered presentations in fixed universes; ordinary simplicial homotopy supplied by AlgebraicTopology.

sources.match: Supplies the homotopy-pro-group model, including the nonfunctorial factorization qualification.

proofSteps: Import the proper simplicial Kan–Quillen model from the existing topology owner, including the ordinary obstruction theory requested there.
Use cofinite reindexing and finite predecessor matching objects. The increasing connectivity bound gives Isaksen’s strong fibrations (Definition 6.5).

Apply the two factorizations and lifting theorem, I01 Propositions 15.1, 15.2, 15.4; then the pushout-product argument of §16. Properness is isolated in the next target because its original proof needs the published correction.

nodes.title: Properness and strong fibrations
nodes.statement: Isaksen’s model structure is left and right proper. A strong fibration is a fibration, and arbitrary fibrations are retracts of suitable strong-fibration presentations. Consequently pullback along a fibration preserves weak equivalences, also for maps over a fixed pro-space.

proofSteps: Left properness follows from cofibrancy of every object.

For right properness, reduce a fibration to a retract of a strong fibration and use the levelwise connectivity criterion. Read and incorporate the correction in Isaksen 2004 Remark 4.14 before claiming this reduction proved (G1).
Apply the right-proper pullback square; do not substitute the strict model’s weak equivalences.

nodes.title: Connected pointed homotopy detection
nodes.statement: For connected pointed pro-spaces, a pointed map is an Isaksen weak equivalence exactly when it induces an isomorphism of pro-groups π_n for every n≥1. A pointed morphism whose underlying morphism is an isomorphism in the unpointed homotopy category is an isomorphism in the pointed homotopy category.
hypotheses: Small cofiltered presentations in fixed universes; ordinary simplicial homotopy supplied by AlgebraicTopology.

sources.match: Connectedness removes the need to test the other components through homotopy local systems.

proofSteps: Represent the map after cofinite reindexing; use path transport on connected levels to recover all stalks of Π_n from the selected one.
Apply the weak-equivalence criterion, and use the forgetful pointed model functor reflecting weak equivalences for the isomorphism assertion.
acceptance: A map of two-component objects preserving only the chosen component is outside this test.

nodes.title: Local-coefficient detection
nodes.statement: A map f:X→Y of pro-spaces is an Isaksen weak equivalence if and only if π_0(f) is a pro-set isomorphism, Π_1X→f*Π_1Y is an isomorphism of pro-local systems, and H^m(Y,L)→H^m(X,f*L) is an isomorphism for every m≥0 and every abelian local system L on Y. Here cohomology for a system represented on Y_i is the filtered colimit over later levels of ordinary cohomology with pulled-back coefficients; finite constant coefficients alone do not state this criterion.
hypotheses: Small cofiltered presentations in fixed universes; ordinary simplicial homotopy supplied by AlgebraicTopology.

sources.match: The obstruction-theoretic characterization quantifies over all local systems, together with π_0 and Π_1.

proofSteps: A weak equivalence admits a level presentation with connectivity increasing arbitrarily far, so ordinary local-coefficient comparison gives every fixed cohomological degree in the filtered colimit.

Conversely replace by a cofibration and test maps into strongly fibrant objects. A finite Moore–Postnikov lifting tower has obstruction classes in local cohomology; kill each using the assumed isomorphisms.

Pass to the inverse limit of the matching fibrations and use the model’s fibrant retract theorem. The ordinary local-coefficient Whitehead and Moore–Postnikov inputs are explicitly requested from AlgebraicTopology, not asserted by its existing Kan predicate.
acceptance: Keep the integral sign system on S¹ in the test class; do not infer this theorem from a mod-p cohomology comparison.

nodes.title: Coverings of pro-spaces
nodes.statement: A simplicial covering p:E→X has the unique lifting property for every vertex inclusion Δ[0]→Δ[n], including every choice of vertex. A pro-covering is a pro-morphism isomorphic to a levelwise simplicial covering; connected Galois coverings have a levelwise presentation with E_i/Aut_Xi(E_i)≅X_i. Universal pointed coverings are formed from the levelwise universal simplicial coverings. The deck group is a pro-group, not an unqualified single discrete group.
hypotheses: Pointed connected pro-spaces where specified; arbitrary pro-groups, without a hidden finite-index restriction.

sources.locator: Appendix A.1, Definition A.1 and preceding paragraphs, p. 853
sources.match: The unique vertex-lift definition and its levelwise pro-version are stronger than the Kan fibration condition.

proofSteps: Import ordinary simplicial covering theory, compared by realization with the already owned topological universal-cover API; this extension is requested from AlgebraicTopology.
Use D0 reindexing to make a finite covering diagram levelwise. Define the pro-cover property invariantly under pro-isomorphism.
Apply the ordinary pointed universal-cover functor levelwise and retain its transition maps and deck actions.
acceptance: The hypotheses and the indicated canonical map are retained under every use.

nodes.statement: For maps f:X→W and g:Y→W and an isomorphism γ:X≅Y in Ho(Pro(SSet)) with gγ=f, every pro-covering W′→W admits an isomorphism γ′:X×_W W′≅Y×_W W′ in the homotopy category, compatible with γ and the maps to W′. Choices can be made compatibly with morphisms of the covering. If W′/W is connected Galois, the induced cohomology isomorphisms with any constant abelian group A are equivariant for its deck pro-group action. Existence, rather than uniqueness of γ′, is asserted.
hypotheses: Pointed connected pro-spaces where specified; arbitrary pro-groups, without a hidden finite-index restriction.

sources.match: A homotopy equivalence in the slice of the homotopy category can be transported along a covering; its proof supplies deck equivariance.

proofSteps: Replace W by a fibrant object and transport the connected covering category along the equivalence; handle components separately.
Represent γ and the structural homotopy by actual maps into fibrant replacements. Lift that homotopy along the covering to make the maps compatible.
Right properness identifies the strict pullbacks with the required derived pullbacks. Deck transformations commute with these lifted maps, giving equivariance after cohomology.
acceptance: For W′=W choose γ′=γ. Do not claim canonical uniqueness for a general homotopy isomorphism.

nodes.title: Classifying pro-space and fibrant replacement
nodes.statement: For a pro-group G=(G_i) use H.1’s discrete nerves BG_i and EG_i levelwise. On a cofinite directed presentation define G_i* = ∏_{j≤i}G_j, embed G_i by all transition maps (including the identity factor), and set B*G_i=E(G_i*)/G_i for the resulting right action. Then BG→B*G is a levelwise ordinary weak equivalence and B*G is fibrant in the Isaksen pointed model. BG is not declared fibrant merely because each level is Kan.
hypotheses: Pointed connected pro-spaces where specified; arbitrary pro-groups, without a hidden finite-index restriction.

sources.match: Adds a pro-level fibrant replacement to the already owned discrete BG and EG.

proofSteps: Import the discrete free, contractible EG and its quotient; build G* from finite predecessor products.

The diagonal inclusion of G_i into G_i* is injective, and the product projection to predecessor factors is surjective. The associated nerve map is a Kan fibration; this discrete lemma is requested from H.1.
Check the relative matching maps for B*G are co-1-fibrations. Both quotient models have π_1=G_i and no higher groups, so the comparison is a level weak equivalence.
acceptance: The hypotheses and the indicated canonical map are retained under every use.

nodes.title: Homotopy limit and topological homotopy groups
nodes.statement: Let Mat(X) denote the right-derived limit of a small pro-simplicial set, represented by the ordinary homotopy limit of a levelwise Kan diagram. For a pointed X define π_n^top(X,x)=π_n(Mat(X),x), with pointed sets in degree zero. The derived constant/limit adjunction identifies it with Hom_Ho(Pro(SSet)_*)(cS^n,X). Call X path-connected when Mat(X) is path-connected. Its comparison to lim_i π_n(X_i,x_i) is canonical; invertibility requires the separate profiniteness theorem.
hypotheses: Small pointed pro-simplicial diagrams; path-connectedness, profiniteness and surjectivity are required exactly where stated.

sources.match: Uses Postnikov replacement to compare the derived limit for the two pro-space models.
Defines the topological homotopy groups and distinguishes path-connectedness from pro-connectedness.

proofSteps: Constant objects preserve cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, so constant and limit form a Quillen adjunction.
Use I01 Proposition 8.4’s levelwise Kan and Postnikov-tower argument to identify the derived limit with the ordinary homotopy limit.

The requested unstable homotopy-limit interface uses a Reedy fibrant cosimplicial replacement C^q=∏_{i_q→…→i_0}X_i0 and actual Tot_m=Map(sk_m Δ^•,C^•), including all compatibility equations. A single C^m is not Tot_m.
acceptance: The hypotheses and the indicated canonical map are retained under every use.

api.statement: Derived maps cK→X are naturally maps K→Mat(X).

api.name: materialization_reindex
api.statement: Cofinal reindexing and Isaksen weak equivalence preserve Mat up to ordinary weak equivalence.

api.statement: Projections induce natural π_n^top(X)→lim π_n(X_i), with the prescribed low-degree algebra.

tests.name: constant_space
tests.statement: Mat(cK)≃K for a Kan complex K.

tests.name: finite_sets
tests.statement: For a system of finite sets considered as discrete spaces, Mat is the discrete set of compatible tuples and has no positive homotopy groups.

tests.name: tot_not_degree
tests.statement: For the discrete diagram *→{0,1} sending * to 0, a degree-zero choice (*,1) in the cosimplicial replacement has no extension to Tot_1. The compatibility equations exclude it; retaining only independent product coordinates would admit it.

uses.how: Relates topological and pro-homotopy groups.
Produces an ordinary simplicial set from a completed pro-object.

nodes.title: Vanishing of profinite derived limits
nodes.statement: For an inverse system G of finite groups over a small cofiltered category, the nonabelian derived-limit pointed set lim¹G is trivial. For a system A of finite abelian groups, lim^s A=0 for every s≥1. The assertion is invariant under pro-isomorphism, so it applies to profinite pro-groups represented by finite groups, without assuming countable indexing.
hypotheses: Small pointed pro-simplicial diagrams; path-connectedness, profiniteness and surjectivity are required exactly where stated.

sources.match: Uses finite-predecessor product resolutions and compactness; no Mittag–Leffler tower restriction is inserted.

proofSteps: Pass to a cofinite directed presentation. Embed G_i in G_i*=∏_{j≤i}G_j through all transition maps. Its matching projections are surjective and the product system is derived-limit acyclic.
The finite quotients G_i*/G_i are sets with transitive G_i* action; compactness supplies compatible lifts, giving the nonabelian lim¹ assertion.

In the abelian case use 0→A→A*→A*/A→0, acyclicity of A*, and dimension shifting. The higher derived-limit formalism is included in the topology supplier contract. Current Tau Ceti already supplies inverse-system compactness; do not rebuild it.
acceptance: Use the system Z/p^r to obtain lim¹=0. The unrestricted discrete system Z with multiplication by p is outside the finite/profinite hypothesis and cannot be accepted by this proof.

nodes.title: Homotopy groups of profinite pro-spaces
nodes.statement: If pointed X has π_0(X)=* and every π_n(X), n≥1, is a profinite pro-group, then Mat(X) is path-connected and π_n^top(X)→lim π_n(X) is an isomorphism for all n≥1; the degree-zero comparison is a bijection of singleton pointed sets. No finiteness of the whole simplicial sets or uniform Postnikov bound is assumed.
hypotheses: Small pointed pro-simplicial diagrams; path-connectedness, profiniteness and surjectivity are required exactly where stated.

sources.match: The proof needs the actual partial-totalization tower and the connectivity and complete-convergence hypotheses, recorded in G2.

proofSteps: Apply the genuine Reedy totalization tower. Its fringe spectral sequence has E_2^{s,t}=lim^s π_t(X), with abelian groups for t≥2 and the pointed-set/group interpretations on the low fringe.

Use profinite-derived-limit vanishing. Verify the connectivity and complete-convergence hypotheses for this tower, not only collapse of the displayed E_2 page; this is the explicit unread Bousfield–Kan proof obligation G2.
The edge comparison is induced by the projections, hence agrees with the canonical map and is natural.
acceptance: For X=B(Z/p^r), the materialization is K(Z_p,1) as an ordinary homotopy type; π_1 is the underlying abstract group of the inverse limit, with its profinite topology available separately.
A statement only about inverse limits of π_1 cannot certify path-connectedness or the higher comparisons.

nodes.title: Endpoint-preserving pro-cylinders
nodes.statement: For a pro-simplicial set X with two distinct specified vertices x_0,x_1, form Cyl₂(X) from X×Δ[1] by collapsing each {x_i}×Δ[1] to its own vertex. The endpoint map X⊔_{ {x_0,x_1} }X→Cyl₂(X) is a cofibration and the projection to X is an Isaksen weak equivalence. These maps form a cylinder in the undercategory of the two-point set. The projection need not be a fibration.
hypotheses: Small pointed pro-simplicial diagrams; path-connectedness, profiniteness and surjectivity are required exactly where stated.

sources.locator: Appendix A.2.3, p. 858, corrected cylinder assertion
sources.match: Only a cofibration and a weak equivalence are required; the printed fibration claim has the elementary counterexample recorded in E2.

proofSteps: Construct the quotient levelwise and use ordinary relative simplicial cylinder theory, preserving its two endpoint inclusions.
Each quotient projection contracts the interval relative to the two selected vertices in the ordinary homotopy sense, so the pro-projection is a weak equivalence.
Use this cylinder only for cofibrant domains in the undercategory; the interval with its two distinct endpoints supplies the domain for paths.
acceptance: The hypotheses and the indicated canonical map are retained under every use.

api.name: cylinder_endpoint_cofibration
api.statement: The combined endpoint inclusion is a cofibration in the two-point undercategory.

api.name: cylinder_projection_weakEquivalence
api.statement: The projection is a weak equivalence and composes with either endpoint to the identity.

api.name: path_relative_homotopy
api.statement: Maps from Δ[1] into a fibrant target modulo this cylinder give endpoint-preserving path classes.

tests.name: two_points_cylinder
tests.statement: For X={x_0,x_1}, Cyl₂(X) is X and the projection is the identity.

tests.name: third_point_interval
tests.statement: For X={x_0,x_1,a}, Cyl₂(X) is two isolated vertices together with Δ[1] over a. This projection is not a Kan fibration: a Kan horn witnessing an inverse to the directed edge has no filler.

tests.name: fixed_endpoints
tests.statement: For X=Δ[1] with its endpoints, a homotopy fixes both endpoints at every time, as required for ordinary relative path homotopy.

uses.how: Defines the path groupoid in the homotopy category without a false fibration assertion.

nodes.title: Monodromy on pointed mapping classes
nodes.statement: For pointed pro-spaces X and two points y_0,y_1 of Y, a path class u:y_0→y_1 in Mat(Y) induces a bijection u_*:Hom_Ho(Pro(SSet)_*)(X,(Y,y_0))→Hom(X,(Y,y_1)). Identity paths act identically and composition of paths composes these bijections. At y_0=y_1 this is the π_1^top(Y,y_0) action. Use the convention for which the induced action on fundamental-group homomorphisms is φ↦αφα⁻¹.
hypotheses: Small pointed pro-simplicial diagrams; path-connectedness, profiniteness and surjectivity are required exactly where stated.

sources.locator: Lemma A.9 and Lemma A.12, pp. 858–860
sources.match: Lifting a path in a fibrant replacement defines monodromy and identifies its group action with target conjugation.

proofSteps: Replace Y by a fibrant target. Extend the pair consisting of f:X→Y and the path u along X∨Δ[1]→X×Δ[1], a trivial cofibration.
The terminal restriction gives a pointed map to (Y,y_1). Use relative homotopies to prove independence of extension, representative path and fibrant replacement.
Concatenation and inversion prove the action laws. Compare the induced map of loops with conjugation using the same path-order convention.
acceptance: The hypotheses and the indicated canonical map are retained under every use.

api.name: transport_id
api.statement: Transport along the constant path fixes every pointed class.

api.name: transport_comp
api.statement: Transport along a composite equals successive transport.

api.name: transport_pi1
api.statement: For a loop α, the induced π_1 homomorphism is αφα⁻¹.

api.name: transport_natural
api.statement: Transport is natural under pointed source maps and target maps carrying the chosen path.

tests.name: BG_conjugation
tests.statement: For X=BC₂,Y=BS₃, a transposition homomorphism is transported to each of its conjugates in S₃.

tests.name: abelian_target
tests.statement: For X=S¹,Y=BC₃, loop transport fixes each homomorphism Z→C₃.

tests.name: transport_empty_paths
tests.statement: For a constant two-point target, distinct points have no connecting path; no transport bijection between those basepoints is postulated.

uses.how: Describes the fibers of forgetting the point.
Identifies the geometric fundamental-group action on arithmetic mapping classes.

nodes.title: Pointed maps modulo monodromy
nodes.statement: If Y is path-connected, forgetting points induces a bijection Hom_Ho(Pro(SSet)_*)(X,Y)/π_1^top(Y)≅Hom_Ho(Pro(SSet))(X,Y), for any pointed X.
hypotheses: Small pointed pro-simplicial diagrams; path-connectedness, profiniteness and surjectivity are required exactly where stated.

sources.match: The quotient computes unpointed maps when the target is path-connected.

proofSteps: Represent an unpointed map into a fibrant target; connect its image of the source point to the target point and transport.
An unpointed homotopy has a basepoint track; its loop is precisely the orbit ambiguity, proving injectivity of the orbit map.
acceptance: For BC₂→BS₃, the trivial homomorphism and the conjugacy class of transposition homomorphisms give exactly two unpointed classes.

nodes.title: Pointed lifts of unpointed isomorphisms
nodes.statement: If pointed X is unpointedly isomorphic to connected pointed Y and every π_n(Y), n≥1, is a profinite pro-group, every such unpointed isomorphism admits a pointed isomorphism lift.
hypotheses: Small pointed pro-simplicial diagrams; path-connectedness, profiniteness and surjectivity are required exactly where stated.

sources.match: Profiniteness provides path-connectedness and the pointed lift reflects invertibility.

proofSteps: EH.2’s profinite homotopy-limit theorem gives paths between the necessary points.
The absolute orbit theorem supplies a pointed lift, whose underlying unpointed isomorphism makes it a pointed isomorphism.
acceptance: The lift need not be unique, and forgetting the pro-connected/profinite hypotheses is not justified.

nodes.title: Pointed lifting over a base
nodes.statement: Let pointed X,Y map to pointed B. If Y and B are path-connected and π_1^top(Y)→π_1^top(B) is surjective, forgetting points gives a surjection from Hom in Ho(Pro(SSet)_*)↓(B,b) to Hom in Ho(Pro(SSet))↓B. These are slices of homotopy categories: their structural triangles commute as morphism classes; no chosen null-homotopy is part of a morphism.
hypotheses: Small pointed pro-simplicial diagrams; path-connectedness, profiniteness and surjectivity are required exactly where stated.

sources.match: A loop lifted from B corrects a pointed representative so its structural triangle commutes in the pointed homotopy category.

proofSteps: Lift the underlying unpointed map to a pointed one using target path-connectedness.
The two composites to B differ by a loop at b. Surjectivity on topological π_1 lifts that loop to Y.
Transport by its inverse to obtain a pointed map in the relative Hom set.
acceptance: For B=* this recovers the absolute surjection. Replacing the source with Ho(Pro(SSet)_*/B) changes the mapping problem and fails the stated interface.

nodes.title: Relative isomorphisms lift
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of relative-surjection, any isomorphism in Ho(Pro(SSet))↓B has a preimage that is an isomorphism in Ho(Pro(SSet)_*)↓(B,b).
hypotheses: Small pointed pro-simplicial diagrams; path-connectedness, profiniteness and surjectivity are required exactly where stated.

sources.match: The pointed lift reflects invertibility on underlying homotopy types.

proofSteps: Use relative-surjection to lift the given map.
Its underlying unpointed map is an isomorphism, so it is an isomorphism in the pointed homotopy category. The inverse also commutes with the structure map because the original triangle does.
acceptance: No uniqueness of the lift or of its pointed inverse class beyond ordinary categorical inversion is claimed.

nodes.title: Stabilizer quotient for relative maps
nodes.statement: With the same hypotheses, let S_X⊂π_1^top(B,b) be the stabilizer of the pointed structure class p_X under monodromy, and Δ_XY its preimage under π_1^top(Y,y)→π_1^top(B,b). Monodromy restricts to the pointed relative Hom set, and its Δ_XY-orbits biject with Hom_Ho(Pro(SSet))↓B(X,Y). The whole π_1(Y) need not preserve the relative subset.
hypotheses: Small pointed pro-simplicial diagrams; path-connectedness, profiniteness and surjectivity are required exactly where stated.

sources.match: The correct relative quotient uses the preimage of the structural-map stabilizer.

proofSteps: Naturality of path transport identifies the loops preserving the structural triangle with Δ_XY.
Use the absolute orbit theorem to characterize pairs with the same unpointed class; the relative constraint forces the loop into Δ_XY.
Use the relative surjection for existence, giving the claimed bijection.
acceptance: For B=*, Δ_XY=π_1^top(Y). For X=B=BG with identity structure, its stabilizer is Z(G); when G=S₃ this stabilizer is trivial, so replacing Δ by the full π_1(Y) would be wrong.

nodes.title: Rigid étale covers
nodes.statement: For a locally noetherian scheme X in a fixed universe, a rigid cover is a disjoint union U=∐_x U_x indexed by its geometric points in the chosen small presentation, each U_x connected, étale and separated over X, with a specified lift u_x of x. Morphisms preserve these lifts. The geometric-point presentation and its universe enlargement comparisons are retained. A rigid pullback along f:X→Y uses the component of X×_Y U_f(x) containing the specified lifted point, separately for every x; this may repeat a component of the ordinary pullback.
hypotheses: Locally noetherian schemes, degreewise for simplicial schemes; all finite-type, geometric-unibranch and characteristic restrictions in the statement are retained.

sources.match: The separated, connected pointed pieces make maps unique; rigid pullback is not ordinary base change.

proofSteps: Use the small étale site and a size-controlled geometric-point indexing family; existence of connected components as open subschemes follows from local noetherianity.
Take connected pointed components of the ordinary fiber products. A point-preserving map between connected étale separated neighborhoods is unique.
Prove the rigid pullback universal property. Size and choice compatibility are part of supplier contract R1, rather than a claim that a class of all geometric points is a small set.
acceptance: The hypotheses and the indicated canonical map are retained under every use.

api.name: rigidCover_map_unique
api.statement: There is at most one rigid cover map over a fixed base map.

api.name: rigidPullback_lift
api.statement: Rigid maps V→f*U over Z→X correspond to rigid maps V→U over Z→Y.

api.name: rigidPullback_comp
api.statement: Iterated rigid pullback agrees, by its canonical isomorphism, with pullback along the composite.

api.name: rigidCover_etale
api.statement: Each chosen connected piece is separated étale; the disjoint union is a covering family, with no finite-component requirement.

tests.name: chosen_algebraic_point
tests.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, a connected étale neighborhood of the canonical point is Spec of that field and its chosen lift is unique.

tests.name: repeat_components
tests.statement: For A¹_C→Spec C and the canonical point cover of Spec C, ordinary pullback has one connected component A¹_C. Rigid pullback has a separate copy for each geometric point of A¹_C, including distinct copies chosen at 0 and 1. Replacing it by the ordinary pullback loses the rigid data.

tests.name: finite_not_required
tests.statement: On A¹_C the indexing includes its infinitely many complex closed points; a definition demanding a finite index family would reject the required rigid covers.

uses.how: Supplies matching covers and their rigid pullbacks.
Ensures functoriality survives algebraic field automorphisms.

nodes.title: Rigid hypercovers of simplicial schemes
nodes.statement: A rigid hypercover U_•→X of a scheme is an augmented simplicial scheme whose map U_n→(cosk^X_{n−1}U)_n is a rigid cover for every n≥0, with U_0→X in degree zero. For simplicial X_• use an augmented bisimplicial U_{a,b}, with U_{a,−1}=X_a, whose rows are rigid hypercovers and whose maps in a preserve the rigid lifts. HRR(X_•) has at most one map between any two objects, is nonempty and cofiltered, and admits rigid pullbacks along simplicial scheme maps. Generic hypercovers and descent remain E2’s construction.
hypotheses: Locally noetherian schemes, degreewise for simplicial schemes; all finite-type, geometric-unibranch and characteristic restrictions in the statement are retained.

sources.locator: Definitions 6.2–6.4, pp. 16–17; Proposition 6.10, pp. 17–18; Proposition 6.14 and 6.17, pp. 19–20
sources.match: The rigid matching data and rigid limits supply the cofiltered indexing and finite-degree cofinality used by the diagonal.

proofSteps: Use E2’s augmented matching-object convention. Recursively choose rigid covers; the split degeneracies are constructed through latching components with their specified points.
For finite diagrams form rigid limits by taking the connected pointed components of the ordinary matching fiber products; include the induced degeneracies, as in IEt Remarks 6.9 and 6.13.
The rigid-limit universal property supplies cones and uniqueness supplies equalizers. A finite-degree right Kan construction gives cofinality into ∏_{a≤m}HRR(X_a), for every m.
acceptance: The hypotheses and the indicated canonical map are retained under every use.

api.name: rigidHypercover_degree_zero
api.statement: The first matching map is the rigid cover U_0→X, never an omitted condition.

api.name: rigidHypercover_pullback
api.statement: Rigid pullback preserves matching covers and has the universal property of IEt Proposition 6.10.

api.name: HRR_cofiltered
api.statement: The size-controlled HRR index is nonempty and cofiltered.

api.name: HRR_finite_degree_cofinal
api.statement: For every finite m, HRR(X_•)→∏_{a≤m}HRR(X_a) is cofinal.

tests.name: cech_refinement
tests.statement: An étale Čech hypercover admits rigid refinements compatible with its specified point lifts; its degree-one matching map is to U_0×_X U_0.

tests.name: missing_degree_zero
tests.statement: The empty augmented simplicial object over a nonempty scheme is not a rigid hypercover, even if all its positive-degree conditions are vacuous.

tests.name: constant_scheme
tests.statement: HRR(X) and HRR(cX) yield equivalent indexing systems; the diagonal construction on a constant scheme recovers the ordinary étale type.

uses.how: Makes the diagonal component systems into pro-objects.
Gives common refinements for the analytic comparison maps.

nodes.title: Rigid étale topological type
nodes.statement: For a degreewise locally noetherian simplicial scheme X_• define Et(X_•) by the pro-system U↦diag π_0(U_{a,b}), U∈HRR(X_•). For an ordinary scheme use its constant simplicial object. A compatible geometric point determines a vertex of this pro-object. Rigid pullback gives functorial maps, compatible with compositions through the rigid universal isomorphisms. Define raw étale π_n by EH.0’s pro-homotopy groups; the finite-étale profinite group is a separate comparison, not its definition.
hypotheses: Locally noetherian schemes, degreewise for simplicial schemes; all finite-type, geometric-unibranch and characteristic restrictions in the statement are retained.

sources.locator: §3, pp. 8–10, definitions of Et and sEt; Propositions 3.1–3.2 and Theorem 3.3
sources.match: The simultaneous rigid system and its diagonal differ as pro-objects from merely realizing the degreewise pro-types, although the latter maps by weak equivalence.
Uses the simultaneous bisimplicial rigid cover diagonal for a simplicial variety.

proofSteps: Apply π_0 to each scheme in a rigid bisimplicial hypercover and take the diagonal n↦π_0(U_n,n).
Use the universal rigid pullback to give an index functor and the comparison map of diagrams. Track the canonical coherence isomorphisms in any strictification.
Finite-degree cofinality controls the skeleta. It gives the IEt comparison to the realization of the degreewise pro-types, without declaring those pro-objects strictly isomorphic.
acceptance: The hypotheses and the indicated canonical map are retained under every use.

api.name: etaleType_map
api.statement: Every scheme map induces a pro-map, with identity and composition after the chosen coherence identifications.

api.name: etaleType_point
api.statement: A geometric basepoint yields a compatible pro-vertex and pointed maps for point-preserving morphisms.

api.name: etaleType_constant
api.statement: The constant simplicial scheme construction agrees with the ordinary rigid étale type.

api.name: etaleType_coproduct
api.statement: Et sends disjoint unions to coproducts in pro-spaces; materialization or completion is not inferred to preserve these coproducts.

tests.name: separably_closed_type
tests.statement: For separably closed k, Et(Spec k) is weakly contractible.

tests.name: finite_field_type
tests.statement: For F_q, Et(Spec F_q)≃B Gal(F_q^sep/F_q) with Gal≅Zhat as a pro-group, not constant discrete Z.

tests.name: simplicial_Cp
tests.statement: For the simplicial C-scheme B(C_p), the raw diagonal has the homotopy type BC_p. Replacing X_• by X_0 would give a point and is wrong.

uses.how: Supplies all raw étale mapping classes and finite-cover transport.
Supplies the input to p-completion, before materialization.

nodes.title: Cohomology of the rigid étale type
nodes.statement: For locally noetherian X, the rigid type has H^m(Et(X),L)≅H^m_et(X,L) for locally constant abelian étale sheaves L in the ordinary étale local-system range, naturally in X, L and every m≥0. This includes arbitrary constant abelian groups, not only finite groups. For a degreewise locally noetherian simplicial scheme, constant finite coefficients have the corresponding total/diagonal comparison. It uses the same native sheaf cohomology and the E2 bounded-below descent comparison.
hypotheses: Locally noetherian schemes, degreewise for simplicial schemes; all finite-type, geometric-unibranch and characteristic restrictions in the statement are retained.

sources.locator: §2 after Theorem 2.10, p. 7, citing Friedlander Proposition 5.9; §3, pp. 8–10
sources.match: States the cohomology comparison but the full arbitrary-local-system proof and range remain reading obligation G3.
The geometric Galois-cohomology transport uses all constant abelian groups.

proofSteps: Compare the local system on the simplicial component diagram with its pullback to the hypercover’s étale site.

Use E2’s bounded-below hypercover descent for the sheaf concentrated in degree zero, and take the filtered colimit over refinements. This requires the local-system acyclicity/refinement theorem, not the false claim that any cover is acyclic.

Read the proof and precise coefficient range of Friedlander Proposition 5.9 or a primary public replacement (G3); IEt’s citation alone does not close this step. Finite-degree descent then compares total and diagonal constant-coefficient cohomology.
acceptance: For separably closed k and constant A, H^0=A and H^m=0 for m>0. For a field, compare with SF.2/etale-galois-comparison; do not claim vanishing of higher Galois cohomology.

nodes.title: Raw and finite étale homotopy groups
nodes.statement: For connected locally noetherian X the profinite completion of the raw pro-group π_1(Et(X),x) identifies with IG.0’s finite-étale fundamental group, compatibly with finite-cover fibers. If X is noetherian and geometrically unibranch, each raw π_n, n≥1, is a profinite pro-group, and π_1 itself identifies with that finite-étale group in Pro(Grp). For a field this identifies Et(Spec k) with BG_k in the raw homotopy category.
hypotheses: Locally noetherian schemes, degreewise for simplicial schemes; all finite-type, geometric-unibranch and characteristic restrictions in the statement are retained.

sources.locator: Notation before §2, p. 822; Appendix A.3, pp. 862–866
sources.match: Separates raw SGA3-type π_1 from its finite-étale completion and invokes Artin–Mazur Theorem 11.1 for geometric-unibranch profiniteness.

proofSteps: Use the finite-cover classification of the rigid type and the geometric fiber to identify finite quotients of the raw π_1 with finite étale covers.
For geometric-unibranch noetherian schemes invoke the precise Artin–Mazur Theorem 11.1; its proof is unread and remains G4. Do not replace it by the abstract compactness of finite groups.
For a field use the finite Galois hypercover system to model Et by BG_k, equivalently the field’s higher asphericity. NC.0 owns the cohomological field conclusion.
acceptance: A non-unibranch nodal rational curve may have a nonprofinite raw fundamental pro-group; finite completion must remain explicit. The pro-étale Noohi group is another construction and is not substituted here.

nodes.title: Finite étale base change
nodes.statement: For finite étale W′→W between locally noetherian schemes, Et(W′)→Et(W) is a finite pro-covering. For every X→W in this scope the natural map Et(X×_W W′)→Et(X)×_{Et(W)}Et(W′) is an isomorphism of pro-simplicial sets. Consequently a relative homotopy isomorphism Et(X)≅Et(Y) over Et(W) lifts along W′, compatibly with projections, with the existence and deck-equivariance qualifications of EH.1.
hypotheses: Locally noetherian schemes, degreewise for simplicial schemes; all finite-type, geometric-unibranch and characteristic restrictions in the statement are retained.

sources.match: Refines the rigid index until the finite cover splits on every connected piece; the resulting comparison is an actual pro-isomorphism.

proofSteps: For constant degree d, refine rigid covers so W′ splits as d copies on every connected hypercover piece. Treat varying finite degree on its open-and-closed degree loci.
On this cofinal system π_0(U×_W W′)→π_0(U) is a simplicial degree-d covering and the base-change square of component simplicial sets is cartesian.
Pass to the pro-system. Apply EH.1’s covering base-change result to homotopy isomorphisms; this final application adds no uniqueness assertion.
acceptance: For the trivial d-fold cover the type is the d-fold disjoint union at each split level. For a connected quadratic field extension, the associated BG map is a covering of degree two rather than an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Galois-equivariant geometric cohomology transport
nodes.statement: If k-varieties X,Y have Et(X)≅Et(Y) in Ho(Pro(SSet))↓Et(k), then for every abelian group A and every m≥0 there is an isomorphism H^m_et(Y_kbar,A)→H^m_et(X_kbar,A) of G_k-modules, natural in A. Here kbar is a fixed separable closure (or its algebraic closure with the purely inseparable étale comparison). The isomorphism is induced by the lifted finite-cover system; an abstract group isomorphism alone is insufficient.
hypotheses: Locally noetherian schemes, degreewise for simplicial schemes; all finite-type, geometric-unibranch and characteristic restrictions in the statement are retained.

sources.match: The finite-extension covering tower, its deck action and affine-limit cohomology give the geometric Galois-module isomorphism.

proofSteps: Apply EH.1 covering base change once to the pro-covering of Et(k) formed by the entire pointed finite Galois extension tower. This supplies an isomorphism of the pulled-back towers compatible with their deck action; unrelated choices of finite-cover lifts would not suffice.
Apply cohomology of the rigid type to this tower, keeping homotopy invariance for arbitrary constant abelian A and the deck-equivariant projection maps.

Take the filtered colimit of scheme cohomology along the affine field-extension system. SF.2’s limit theorem identifies this with the geometric cohomology, and the deck actions give the actual G_k action.
acceptance: For X=Y and the identity choose the identity on cohomology. Infinite A is still in scope; a finite-coefficient Artin comparison cannot replace G3.

nodes.title: Étale homotopy sequence for elementary fibrations
nodes.statement: Let f:X→Y be an elementary fibration of smooth connected varieties in characteristic zero, with affine curve fibers, and geometric x↦y. Form the cofiltered pointed finite étale Galois cover system 𝒴 of Y and 𝒳=X×_Y𝒴. The geometric fiber, 𝒳 and 𝒴 have the Friedlander homotopy fiber sequence with all primes; finite-cover invariance identifies its higher groups with those of X and Y. This gives …→π_n Et(X_y)→π_n Et(X)→π_n Et(Y)→π_{n−1}Et(X_y)→… in the appropriate pro-group ranges. In particular, when Y is raw K(π,1), its low-degree part is 1→π_1 Et(X_y)→π_1 Et(X)→π_1 Et(Y)→1.
hypotheses: Locally noetherian schemes, degreewise for simplicial schemes; all finite-type, geometric-unibranch and characteristic restrictions in the statement are retained.

sources.locator: Notation before §2, p. 822; Proposition 2.8, pp. 827–828, invoking Friedlander Theorem 11.5
sources.match: Supplies the exact geometric hypotheses and cover-system reduction; the cited homotopy-fiber theorem is G5.

proofSteps: Import the geometric elementary-fibration input from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0: a smooth proper geometrically connected curve family with finite étale boundary and nonempty affine complement fibers. NC.0’s K(pi,1) application consumes this homotopy sequence; it cannot supply the foundational sequence in return.

Over the pointed finite Galois covers, use Friedlander Theorem 11.5’s all-prime homotopy-fiber comparison (unread, G5). Its π_1 trivialization and finite-cover invariance give the claimed higher terms.

The low-degree injectivity requires π_2(Y)=0. NC.0 owns the deduction that X is K(π,1) when its affine-curve fibers and Y are K(π,1); do not derive the full sequence from the arithmetic π_1 exact sequence alone.

nodes.title: Pointed arithmetic lifting
nodes.statement: Let X,Y be connected finite-type k-varieties, with Y geometrically connected and geometrically unibranch. Choose geometric points over one separably closed extension of k and its induced separable closure kbar. The forgetful map Hom_Ho(Pro(SSet)_*)↓Et(k)(Et(X),Et(Y))→Hom_Ho(Pro(SSet))↓Et(k)(Et(X),Et(Y)) is surjective.
hypotheses: X and Y are connected finite-type varieties over the same field.
Y is geometrically connected and geometrically unibranch; X need not be geometrically unibranch.

sources.match: The geometric connectedness of Y makes its arithmetic fundamental-group map surjective; profiniteness gives the required topological path and loop comparisons.

proofSteps: Identify Et(k) with BG_k. Geometric unibranchness of the noetherian Y makes its homotopy pro-groups profinite, so EH.2 gives path-connected materializations.
Import the geometric/arithmetic fundamental-group exact sequence from IG.1; apply the relative lifting theorem and its isomorphism assertion.
acceptance: The relative category is the slice of the homotopy category. Connectedness of Y over k alone cannot replace geometric connectedness.

nodes.statement: Under arithmetic-pointed-lift’s hypotheses, every isomorphism over Et(k) in the unpointed homotopy category has a pointed isomorphism lift over (Et(k),kbar).
hypotheses: X and Y are connected finite-type varieties over the same field.
Y is geometrically connected and geometrically unibranch; X need not be geometrically unibranch.
Geometric basepoints are chosen over one separably closed extension, as in arithmetic-pointed-lift.

proofSteps: Apply the relative isomorphism-lifting theorem using the same profinite and geometric-connectivity verifications as arithmetic-pointed-lift.
acceptance: No canonical choice of pointed lift is asserted.

nodes.title: Geometric monodromy quotient
nodes.statement: Under arithmetic-pointed-lift’s hypotheses, π_1^et(Y_kbar,y) acts on pointed relative mapping classes, and forgetting points induces a surjection from its orbit set to the unpointed relative Hom set. This action is through the actual underlying abstract geometric fundamental group identified by EH.2, not through its finite quotients one at a time.
hypotheses: X and Y are connected finite-type varieties over the same field.
Y is geometrically connected and geometrically unibranch; X need not be geometrically unibranch.
Geometric basepoints are chosen over one separably closed extension, as in arithmetic-pointed-lift.

sources.match: The geometric group is the kernel of the arithmetic map and is contained in the relative stabilizer preimage.

proofSteps: The exact fundamental-group sequence identifies the geometric group with the kernel of π_1(Y)→G_k.
The kernel maps to the identity of G_k and therefore preserves the pointed structure class. It is contained in Δ_XY from the relative orbit theorem.
The relative pointed lifting surjection descends through this subgroup quotient; it need not yet be injective.
acceptance: For k separably closed this reduces to the absolute target-loop orbit formula.

nodes.title: Arithmetic orbit bijection
nodes.statement: Under arithmetic-pointed-lift’s hypotheses, if every open subgroup of G_k has trivial center, the geometric orbit surjection is bijective. The center condition is the strongly center-free predicate owned by IG.1, with all open subgroups included.
hypotheses: X and Y are connected finite-type varieties over the same field.
Y is geometrically connected and geometrically unibranch; X need not be geometrically unibranch.
Geometric basepoints are chosen over one separably closed extension, as in arithmetic-pointed-lift.
Every open subgroup of the absolute Galois group G_k has trivial center.

sources.match: Triviality of the structure-class stabilizer follows by centralizing an open arithmetic image.

proofSteps: If g stabilizes the structure class of Et(X)→BG_k, the conjugation formula says that g centralizes the image U of the raw pro-fundamental group in G_k.

The finite-type connected-variety openness theorem requested from IG.1 says that U is open, including when X is not geometrically unibranch. The open subgroup generated by U and g has g in its center, so g=1.
Thus S_X=1 and Δ_XY is exactly the geometric kernel. Apply the relative orbit theorem.
acceptance: Trivial center of G_k alone is not the supplied hypothesis: the argument uses the center of the open subgroup generated by U and g. No automatic triviality of the geometric-group action is claimed.

nodes.title: Outer fundamental-group map
nodes.statement: Under arithmetic-pointed-lift’s hypotheses and strongly center-free G_k, applying π_1 to a pointed relative class and quotienting by target geometric conjugation yields a basepoint-independent map from unpointed relative homotopy classes to Hom_out,Gk(π_1^et(X),π_1^et(Y)). Here π_1^et(X) may first be a raw pro-group; because the target is profinite each map factors uniquely through X’s finite-étale profinite completion. This map agrees with the usual outer arithmetic homomorphism of a scheme map.
hypotheses: X and Y are connected finite-type varieties over the same field.
Y is geometrically connected and geometrically unibranch; X need not be geometrically unibranch.
Geometric basepoints are chosen over one separably closed extension, as in arithmetic-pointed-lift.
Every open subgroup of the absolute Galois group G_k has trivial center.

sources.match: The conjugation action on π_1 is compatible with geometric monodromy, so the map descends through the same orbit quotient.

proofSteps: Use the native Pro(Grp) functor and the profinite-completion universal property imported from IG.0/IG.1.
Path transport acts on the group homomorphism by conjugation by precisely the geometric target group. The supplier’s outer Hom quotient therefore receives a well-defined orbit map.
Apply the arithmetic orbit bijection. Compare scheme morphisms before taking either quotient, and use the usual geometric-basepoint path torsors for independence.
acceptance: For X=Spec k and a rational point of Y this gives its arithmetic section up to geometric conjugation. It does not give an arbitrary chosen section homomorphism from the unpointed class.

nodes.title: Open-image orbit bijection
nodes.statement: Under arithmetic-pointed-lift’s hypotheses and strongly center-free G_k, the arithmetic orbit bijection restricts to pointed relative classes inducing homomorphisms with open image, modulo π_1(Y_kbar), and unpointed π_1-open relative classes. Openness is tested in the target profinite topology after the finite-étale completion of the source.
hypotheses: X and Y are connected finite-type varieties over the same field.
Y is geometrically connected and geometrically unibranch; X need not be geometrically unibranch.

Every open subgroup of the absolute Galois group G_k has trivial center.

sources.match: Conjugation preserves open images, so the orbit bijection restricts to this invariant subset.

proofSteps: The supplier’s continuous conjugation automorphisms preserve open subgroups. Hence π_1-openness is constant on every geometric orbit.
Restrict the established bijection to that invariant predicate. Its definition agrees on the unpointed side by outer-map-factorization.
acceptance: A surjective fundamental-group map is open. The trivial image in an infinite profinite target need not be open; no set-theoretic image test suffices.

nodes.title: Maps into products of étale K(pi,1) varieties
nodes.statement: Let k have characteristic zero and strongly center-free G_k. Let Y_1,Y_2 be geometrically connected, geometrically unibranch k-varieties whose raw higher étale homotopy pro-groups vanish. For every k-variety X, projections give a bijection Hom_Ho(Pro(SSet))↓Et(k)(Et(X),Et(Y_1×_kY_2))≅Hom(Et(X),Et(Y_1))×Hom(Et(X),Et(Y_2)).
hypotheses: The field k has characteristic zero and every open subgroup of G_k has trivial center.
Y_1 and Y_2 are geometrically connected and geometrically unibranch, with vanishing raw higher étale homotopy pro-groups.
X is any finite-type k-variety; its connected components are treated separately.

sources.match: Uses raw asphericity of the product, the arithmetic fundamental-group fiber product, and the product geometric-conjugation action.

proofSteps: Reduce X to its finitely many connected components. Import NC.0’s characteristic-zero K(pi,1) product theorem and its raw/cohomological bridge.
Use IG.1’s characteristic-zero product formula π_1(Y_1×Y_2)=π_1(Y_1)×_Gkπ_1(Y_2). EH.1’s full faithfulness for B gives the pointed relative Hom product.
The geometric target group is the product of the two geometric groups. The product action quotient is the product of orbit quotients; apply the arithmetic orbit bijections.
acceptance: Use two hyperbolic smooth curves supplied by NC.0. The source X need not itself be K(pi,1), and the target hypothesis cannot be replaced with vanishing of H¹ alone.

nodes.title: Algebraic evaluation of singular simplices
nodes.statement: For compact Hausdorff T put C(T,C) for the existing complex algebra of continuous functions, with the ordinary Euclidean topology on C. For a quasi-projective complex scheme X, evaluation T→Spec(C(T,C))(C) induces a natural bijection Hom_C(Spec C(T,C),X)≅C(T,X(C)_an). It is natural in continuous maps of T and in algebraic maps of X. In particular T=Δⁿ identifies the algebraic formula for singular n-simplices with Mathlib’s native singular simplices, including its universe lift.
hypotheses: T is compact Hausdorff.
X is quasi-projective over C, with the analytic topology supplied by ComplexComparison.

sources.locator: Lemma A.7 and proof, p. 306; Definition A.8, p. 307
sources.match: Affine evaluation and a finite partition-of-unity gluing recover the analytic singular-simplex functor.

proofSteps: For affine X the bijection is the ordinary algebra-homomorphism/point correspondence, with its coordinatewise continuity.

For general quasi-projective X choose a finite partition of unity on T subordinate to the inverse images of an affine cover. Use supports to extend suitable coordinate products by zero and obtain maps on distinguished opens of Spec C(T,C).

Glue the scheme maps and verify uniqueness on the distinguished cover. The support/denominator argument must justify each extension; treating an arbitrary unbounded continuous function times a partition function as automatically continuous at the boundary is not enough.
Precomposition of continuous functions commutes with evaluation. The imported analytification carrier and its affine coordinate tests identify the native singular set.
acceptance: For X=A¹_C the bijection is exactly C(T,C). For T=* it is the usual complex point set. For X=Spec(C[ε]/ε²), every evaluation sends ε to zero; the statement introduces no replacement analytic carrier.

nodes.title: Betti realization of simplicial varieties
nodes.statement: For a simplicial quasi-projective complex scheme X_•, define Sing_an(X_•)=diag([a],[b])↦Sing_b(X_a(C)_an). Equivalently its n-simplices are X_n(C(Δⁿ,C)). Define D(X_•)_n=X_n(C), with discrete complex points in the second direction; constant singular simplices give D(X_•)→Sing_an(X_•). On a constant scheme this is exactly the existing singular functor on its analytification.
hypotheses: Quasi-projective complex schemes, degreewise for simplicial schemes; compact Hausdorff test spaces and smoothness where stated.

sources.locator: Definition A.8 and preceding identity, p. 307; properties (i)–(ii), p. 305
sources.match: The diagonal synchronizes the scheme and singular directions; the discrete point functor retains the simplicial scheme direction.

proofSteps: Compose the given simplicial analytic space with Mathlib’s singular functor and precompose with the simplex diagonal. No new singular-simplex definition is needed.
Use algebraic evaluation degreewise to identify the diagonal with X_n(C(Δⁿ,C)); check both faces and degeneracies, since both indices move.
Constant simplices define the natural map from the diagonal discrete-point object.
acceptance: The hypotheses and the indicated canonical map are retained under every use.

nodes.title: Betti descent for smooth surjections
nodes.statement: For a smooth surjection U→V of smooth quasi-projective complex varieties, let U_n=U×_V⋯×_V U with n+1 factors. Then Sing_an(U_•)→Sing_an(V) is a weak equivalence. More generally the comparison zigzag uses analytic descent for étale hypercovers of complex varieties, including singular varieties; this second assertion uses local analytic homeomorphisms and the imported topological hypercover theorem, not a manifold assertion for singular V.
hypotheses: Quasi-projective complex schemes, degreewise for simplicial schemes; compact Hausdorff test spaces and smoothness where stated.

sources.locator: Example A.10, p. 311; Appendix A.2.3, pp. 309–310
sources.match: The smooth-surjection case uses submersion local sections; the étale-hypercover case is the one needed for the comparison zigzag.

proofSteps: For smooth U,V, analytification is a surjective submersion, so the differential-geometric local-section theorem supplies local sections.
The Čech nerve of a map with local sections is a topological hypercover. Apply the E2 realization theorem, then the native singular/realization comparison.
For an étale hypercover, use that analytic étale maps are local homeomorphisms. Apply the same E2 theorem degreewise and the bisimplicial diagonal weak-equivalence theorem.
acceptance: For the identity cover the augmentation is an equivalence. For a surjection of sets with inappropriate topologies local sections are not automatic. The source’s claim that arbitrary smooth-surjection source and target are smooth manifolds requires the smoothness hypothesis stated here.

nodes.title: p-finite spaces
nodes.statement: For a prime p, a space is p-finite when π_0 is finite and for every basepoint its positive homotopy groups are finite p-groups and vanish above a uniform finite degree. Regard these as homotopy types, or Kan representatives closed under equivalence. Write Sp_p-fin for their essentially small category and Pro(Sp_p-fin) for its homotopy-coherent pro-category. Arbitrary finite π_1 is not allowed unless it is a p-group; degreewise finiteness of a simplicial model is neither the definition nor a replacement for truncation.
hypotheses: A fixed prime p, declared universe bounds, and the individual finite-type or specified-grading hypotheses; no unrestricted infinite-coproduct preservation.

sources.match: Uses finite components, finite p-group homotopy and an eventual truncation bound.
Identifies the finite test category and its finite homotopy-limit closure.

proofSteps: Use the imported ordinary homotopy groups and truncations to define the full subcategory.
Take a small skeleton in the declared universe. Retain all finite component sets, and compare Kan representatives through the homotopy-coherent localization requested from E0.
Prove finite homotopy-limit closure and use finite Postnikov decompositions with finite p-group actions.

nodes.title: p-profinite completion
nodes.statement: For a pro-space X, construct X^∧_p in Pro(Sp_p-fin) with a unit X→X^∧_p, characterized by equivalences of derived mapping spaces Map(X^∧_p,K)≃Map(X,K) for every p-finite K. Extend this to all p-profinite targets by their limit formula. On a small cofiltered representative, maps to a constant K are the filtered colimit of derived level mapping spaces. In particular the unit preserves continuous F_p cohomology in every degree. Completion is not materialization and is not defined as levelwise group completion alone.
hypotheses: A fixed prime p, declared universe bounds, and the individual finite-type or specified-grading hypotheses; no unrestricted infinite-coproduct preservation.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.2, pp. 4–5; Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.3, pp. 5–6

The test localization has underlying infinity-category Pro(Sp_p-fin).
The unit preserves continuous mod-p cohomology before the homotopy limit is taken.

proofSteps: Use the strict model on Pro(SSet) for this localization. Take the BHH finite test set K_p: finite discrete spaces, BC_p and K(C_p,n) for n≥2.

Apply IC’s test-object localization and its nilpotent fibrant characterization; BHH’s finite-limit closure comparison identifies the result with a system of p-finite types. The model/infinity-category adapter is the separate next target.

The mapping-space unit is the localization universal property; K(F_p,n) gives continuous cohomology preservation. This construction is applied to the raw representative of Et, without equating strict and Isaksen weak equivalences.

Under this equivalence the derived constant/limit adjunction identifies its materialization with the ordinary homotopy limit of a strict fibrant representative. Thus Lurie’s finite-type comparison can be applied to the completion constructed above. This assertion does not identify the strict model with the Isaksen homotopy-pro-group model.

The scheme-functorial construction is a functor of homotopy-coherent types; a strictly functorial chosen simplicial-set model is the separate strictification obligation G7.

nodes.title: Finite-type materialization comparison
nodes.statement: For a p-profinite space P, assume H⁰_cont(P,F_p)=F_p via the unit, H¹_cont(P,F_p)=0, and every H^m_cont(P,F_p) is finite-dimensional. Then P is simply connected of finite type in Lurie’s sense: all its higher homotopy pro-p groups are topologically finitely generated. The projection map H^m_cont(P,F_p)→H^m(Mat(P),F_p) is an isomorphism for every m. Consequently Et_p(X) computes mod-p étale cohomology whenever X has these cohomological properties. A finite number of components is handled one connected component at a time.
hypotheses: A fixed prime p, declared universe bounds, and the individual finite-type or specified-grading hypotheses; no unrestricted infinite-coproduct preservation.

sources.locator: Definition 3.3.2 and Proposition 3.3.8, pp. 82–86; Corollary 3.4.10 and Theorem 3.4.12, pp. 91–93
sources.match: The exact finite-type criterion includes connected H⁰, vanishing H¹ and degreewise finite cohomology.
The materialization step is justified only after its cohomological finiteness conditions are supplied; the theorem-number repair is recorded in E4.

proofSteps: Use the homotopy-coherent adapter to view the completed rigid object as Lurie’s p-profinite P.
Apply Corollary 3.4.10 and Theorem 3.4.12 to obtain simple connectivity and finite type; apply Proposition 3.3.8 to the canonical projection-induced map.
For finite components, completion preserves the finite component decomposition and the limit splits accordingly. Apply the connected assertion componentwise.
acceptance: A countable discrete scheme fails the H⁰ hypothesis. A smooth proper positive-genus curve has nonzero H¹, so this criterion alone proves no materialized comparison for that curve; its raw K(pi,1) theorem remains available. B(C_p) shows the stated conditions are sufficient rather than necessary.

nodes.title: Componentwise p-completed realization
nodes.statement: Given a specified decomposition X_•=∐_{a∈A}X_•,a by open-and-closed simplicial subschemes preserved by every face and degeneracy, define Et_p^gr(X)=∐_a Et_p(X_a). Maps carry each specified summand into a specified target summand, together with the induced map of grading sets. If each summand has H⁰_et=F_p, H¹_et=0 and degreewise finite-dimensional mod-p cohomology, its comparison is an isomorphism, and the graded coproduct computes the full componentwise cohomology, with products over A in cohomology. This is a construction on specified graded objects and does not assert such a decomposition exists functorially for every simplicial scheme.
hypotheses: A fixed prime p, declared universe bounds, and the individual finite-type or specified-grading hypotheses; no unrestricted infinite-coproduct preservation.

sources.locator: Appendix A.2.2–A.2.3, pp. 307–310; graded applications in A.4–A.5, pp. 312–315

Functoriality uses the actual map on grading sets and each component map; it cannot be reconstructed from an arbitrary decomposition of each X_n independently.
The cochain complex of a coproduct is the product of the component cochain complexes. Exactness of products of vector spaces gives the cohomology assertion.

nodes.title: Betti–étale comparison zigzag
nodes.statement: For a simplicial quasi-projective C-scheme X and its rigid hypercovers U, set Z_X=holim_U Sing_an(U), where the analytic realization of U uses the diagonal of all its simplicial directions. There is a natural zigzag Sing_an(X)←Z_X→Et_p(X); the left arrow is a weak equivalence. The right arrow is induced by the component map of every connected singular simplex and the completion unit. For a specified grading use the coproduct of these zigzags on the grades. The resulting homotopy-category map is independent of cofinal refinements.
hypotheses: A fixed prime p, declared universe bounds, and the individual finite-type or specified-grading hypotheses; no unrestricted infinite-coproduct preservation.

sources.match: Uses a compatible hypercover family of analytic-to-component maps and then a homotopy limit, rather than a nonexistent direct canonical lift into every cover.
